name: Sihon
description: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

points: Moses gave unto the children of Gad and of Reuben and unto half the tribe of Manasseh the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with the cities thereof, and they built their cities and folds for sheep.

note.label: Numbers 32: The Inheritance of Reuben and Gad on This Side Jordan

points: Moses declares this law after he had slain Sihon the king of the Amorites. When the Lord told Abraham his seed would serve four hundred years, he set the time of the return by the Amorites: the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.
By this point their iniquity was fulfilled, like Babylon whose sins reached unto heaven, so the Lord loosed Israel to come through the land of the Amorites and slay Sihon their king.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

points: Rise up, pass over the river Arnon: behold, I have given into thine hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle. This recaps Numbers 21, when it was time to destroy the king of the Amorites.

note.label: Deuteronomy 2: Meddle Not With Them, and the Giants That Perished

points: But Sihon would not let Israel pass, for the Lord thy God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into thy hand.

note.label: Deuteronomy 2: Meddle Not With Them, and the Giants That Perished

points: Bashan is about to be conquered, and Og the king of Bashan came out with all his people to battle at Edrei. The Most High said fear him not, for I will deliver him and all his people and his land into thy hand, as was done to Sihon king of the Amorites at Heshbon.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: They utterly destroyed the men, women, and children of every city, as they did unto Sihon king of Heshbon. That command came from the Most High himself; this is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of the Bible, not the invented gospel that says he loves everybody no matter what.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against Israel, and Israel smote them and gave their land for an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh.

note.label: Deuteronomy 29: The Covenant Made with Us Who Were Not There

points: For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you. We heard what your God did to the Egyptians, who were a great and powerful kingdom. When ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed. We saw your God destroy kings, dry up the Red Sea, kill the firstborn of the Egyptians. We know that you have got a real God.

Her faith came by report: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, and what ye did unto Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites whom ye utterly destroyed; and as soon as we had heard it, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man. The Lord had said he would put that spirit on the nations.
The Gibeonites leaned on the fame of the Most High: we have heard all that he did in Egypt, and to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites beyond Jordan.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

points: Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of the children of Gad according to their families: Jazer and all the cities of Gilead, half the land of the children of Ammon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, unto the edge of the sea of Chinnereth on the other side Jordan eastward, the cities and their villages.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: Then Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon: let us pass, we pray thee, through thy land into my place. But Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his coast; he gathered all his people together, pitched in Jahaz, and fought against Israel. They came against Israel; Israel did nothing to them.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

points: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, from Arnon even unto Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto Jordan. That is how Israel got the land of the Amorites: the Lord gave it in battle when they came out against his people.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers
